#805. Toney loses bid to avoid Euro 2028 court clash

Ivan Toney's trial will take place during the Euro 2028 tournament

A bid to move the date of England striker Ivan Toney's assault trial to avoid a clash with Euro 2028 has been refused.

The 30-year-old footballer, from Northampton, is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on 6 December.

Toney denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a trial of up to four days was fixed for 12 June 2028, which is three days into the Uefa Euro 2028 tournament.

He represented England at this summer's World Cup and has made 10 international appearances. It is not yet known if he will be selected for Euro 2028, but the application was made in case.

At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, where Toney did not appear, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: "It came to our attention thatâ¦ there may be potentially a football match called the European Championship in 2028 between 9 June and 9 July."

Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: "We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.

"My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup."

Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a "speculative" application.

He refused the request, saying: "It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed."

The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.

Toney missed out on the latest squad for the country's Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

Junta Imai is in the Department of Diabetes, Metabolism and Endocrinology, Tohoku University Graduate School of Medicine, Aoba-ku, Sendai, Miyagi 980-8575, Japan.

Hundreds of millions of people around the world are affected by diabetes mellitus1. It develops when the activity of insulin, a glucose-lowering hormone secreted by pancreatic β-cells, becomes insufficient to maintain healthy glucose levels in the blood. The condition can be managed with oral medication or by injecting insulin and other metabolic hormones, but the constant need for people with diabetes to manage their lifestyle and blood-glucose levels can impair their quality of life. Therapeutic approaches that monitor and control blood glucose automatically are therefore highly desirable. Writing in Nature, Xiu et al.2 report proof of principle of a bioelectronic device called NeuroAxis that does exactly that in rat models of diabetes.

Starship still has some work to do before it's fully up and running.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running.

The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms.

It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully, nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off.

SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved.

Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company.

"That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes."

The Flight 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX.

And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average.

Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites. And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft, if all goes to plan.

For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment.

Rocket recovery is only part of the reuse equation, of course; there's also refurbishment and reflight. And that gets us back to the "work left to do" discussion, for SpaceX has yet to demonstrate rapid reflight with either Super Heavy or Ship.

The company has reflown Super Heavy vehicles on two separate occasions. Booster 14 initially launched on Flight 7 in January 2025, then lifted off again on Flight 9 in May of that year. Booster 15 flew on Flight 8 and Flight 11, which lifted off in March 2025 and October 2025, respectively.

Several months separated each of these Super Heavy reflights. And SpaceX has yet to reuse a Ship, as it had not caught one during a mission until Saturday.

That could change soon: Before Flight 15 lifted off, Musk said that the company wants to reuse both of its Starship stages. That option may still be on the table for Flight 15's Ship.

And we should expect full reuse to be a priority on Starship test flights over the longer haul, with SpaceX working toward shorter and shorter turnaround times — perhaps until an hourly cadence is in sight, if that goal is indeed achievable.

Over the next few years, most Starship launches will likely be devoted to building out the Starlink V3 and Starmind megaconstellations. But the rocket will also carry people to deep space, if all goes to plan, which will require the checking of another set of boxes.

NASA selected Ship to be the first crewed lunar lander for its Artemis program, which aims to establish a base near the lunar south pole by 2032 or so. Current plans call for Ship to land astronauts in that locale for the first time on the Artemis IV mission, which is targeted to fly in 2028.

SpaceX needs to install a crew cabin and life-support system in Ship to make that happen. The company is working on that now and has made considerable progress, according to NASA. Last month, an agency presentation reported that SpaceX is on target to finish building "Cabin 1," a full-scale ground prototype of Ship's crew cabin, by the end of the year.

There's another hurdle to clear, however. On all deep-space missions, Ship will need to fill up its fuel tanks after launch, at a "depot" that SpaceX will set up in Earth orbit. (Launching Ship with full tanks is not an option, as it would be incredibly heavy in that case.)

The depot will be filled by "tanker" variants of Ship. It's unclear how many tanker visits will be required for each Ship deep-space mission; outside experts have floated numbers as high as 22, while Musk has cited six to eight as a probable range.

Whatever the actual number, Ship will need to demonstrate proficiency with off-Earth refueling, something it has yet to do. And there's more to it than just a simple rendezvous: Ship's engines run on liquid oxygen and liquid methane, so the propellants must be kept extremely cold throughout the process.

We're likely to see the first refueling test relatively soon, as time is of the essence for SpaceX. If the company can't get Ship ready for the Artemis IV moon landing in 2028, NASA may go with another private lander — Blue Origin's Blue Moon, which the agency also contracted for Artemis missions.

All of this is to say that, while Flight 15 was a big success for Starship and SpaceX, there's a lot of work left to do — and a lot for space fans to watch for over the coming weeks and months.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. #802. England defender Carter joins Bay FC after Gotham exit

Jess Carter made 83 appearances across all competitions for Gotham FC

England defender Jess Carter has completed a move to Bay FC after leaving Gotham FC as a free agent.

The 29-year-old has signed a contract that will keep her with Bay FC - a club based in the San Francisco Bay Area - until 2028, with the option for an additional year.

Carter joined New York-side Gotham in July 2024 after a six-year spell with Chelsea that saw her win the Women's Super League on five occasions.

"Coming to Bay FC is a new challenge, and that's something I'm excited about," said Carter.

"I've been fortunate to be part of some successful teams, and I know how much work goes into winning. I'm looking forward to getting to know this group, earning the trust of my team-mates and doing my part to help us move forward."

Carter played in all 30 of Gotham's matches in 2026 as the club won the NWSL Shield - given to the league's regular-season champions.

She also helped Gotham win the NWSL Championship in 2025, when they defeated Washington Spirit in the final.

"Jess has been a big part of what we've accomplished as a club, and we're very thankful for the contributions she's made during her time here," said Yael Averbuch West, the president of football operations for Gotham.

Carter, who has 56 senior England caps, was part of the squad that won the 2022 European Championships, while she appeared in all six games as the Lionesses defended their title last summer.

"Jess has consistently demonstrated her quality in championship-winning environments at both club and international level," said Bay FC's chief football officer Paul Green, who worked with Carter at Chelsea.

"I've seen her development and the professionalism she brings every day. She will bring valuable experience to Bay FC, and we're delighted to welcome her to the club."

The 2027 NWSL regular season kicks off in February.

#801. Jennifer Lopez Addresses "Disappointing" Divorce From Ben Affleck

Nearly two years after Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck finalized their divorce, the "Let's Get Loud" singer looked back at the aftermath of their "disappointing" breakup.

Jennifer Lopez knows that sometimes, love does cost a thing.

Nearly two years after the "On The Floor" singer and Ben Affleck finalized their divorce, she reflected on the weight of their breakup—and whether she's ready to dance again with someone new.

"I'm done with that part of my life," Lopez said on the Nov. 17 episode of Benny Blanco and Lil Dicky's Friends Keep Secrets podcast. "It was such a hard, disappointing last situation on every level. On every level, it was so disappointing. I don't ever want to delve into that."

Though she is focusing on living life single, that doesn't mean she'll never be ready for another great love story, especially after taking a deeper look at her split from the Oscar winner.

"I'm OK with myself," she explained. "I was a serial monogamist, one after the other, trying to find the thing, hoping that this was it."

Now, the 57-year-old—mom to 18-year-old twins Max and Emme with ex-husband Marc Anthony—is getting loud with advice for others navigating divorce.

"Always operate in a way that you'll feel proud of when you look back," she shared. Looking back at her experiences, she added, "Even as painful as some of them were so bad—life-shifting pain and hurt—I can look back and be like, 'I loved completely. I acted in a way that I was proud of as a human. I didn't treat anybody in any way that I would be ashamed of.'"

"I did the best that I could in the moment with what I knew," she continued. "That's my advice for anything because when you go through hard things like that, it's easy to be like, 'F--k this.' You're in so much pain you want to hurt somebody else, or somebody has hurt you so much, but you can't. I've always held myself to that kind of standard."

Since then, Lopez—who filed for divorce from Affleck in August 2024, exactly two years after they got married—has continued to carry what she learned from their breakup and its aftermath.

"Be the best person that you can be right now, every single time, especially when it's hard," she emphasized. "When you say you're strong, I think that's part of it. I can look at these things and be like, 'It's OK. These are experiences in my journey.'"

"I don't know why it was my journey sometimes," she admitted. "Then I realized, no, I'm here to learn something. I finally got to a place where I feel like I've learned it, but it took the f--king house to fall down on top of me to do that."

Looking ahead, the "Let's Get Loud" singer—who was first engaged to Affleck in 2002 before splitting two years later—will be dancing for her papi when the time is right.

"I'm different," she said. "Because it changed me. Because I allowed it to change me. Because I wanted to learn the thing. I was like, 'It's done. I'm not doing this anymore. What are you going to do different?'"

"You can intellectually be a smart person and know things," she explained. "But the knowing is not the thing. It's changing the behavior and the patterns. That's the thing. And that is a conscious action that you have to do. You have to change."

#800. Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future

Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

It's no secret that getting playing time is important to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

Unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.

But when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.

An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.

"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.

"I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can."

A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

Although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

The match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.

One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.

At some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment."

For now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times.

Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars. Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year.

On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit), 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life.

On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event.

By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August.

Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space.

Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten.

"We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement.

While this is the first time that 220P has been seen to outburst, over the years we have witnessed other comets spectacularly brighten out of nowhere.

A recent and well-known example is comet 17P/Holmes, which brightened a million-fold in the fall of 2007 as it rose from magnitude +17 to magnitude +2.8, becoming a welcome naked-eye sight in the constellation of Perseus for many people as they made the evening commute home.

The short 5.5-year orbit of 220P marks it out as a Jupiter-family comet.

"Jupiter-family comets are extremely interesting objects to study because they originate primarily from the Kuiper Belt and the Scattered Disk region, later migrating inward until Jupiter captures them into short-period orbits," said Trigo-Rodríguez.

Studying outbursts such as the two experienced by 220P provides vital clues as to the bulk characteristics of Jupiter-family comets, giving us insight into objects that originated from beyond the orbit of Neptune.

Of particular interest to Trigo-Rodríguez is what we should do were one of these objects ever to be found on a collision course with Earth.

"Particularly we are interested in the tensile strength and nature of comets in the framework of our studies on impact hazards," said Trigo-Rodríguez. "Some comets seem determined to demonstrate that they are fragile enough and perhaps give us the chance to invoke disruptive approaches that might be substantially different from the ones already tested or proposed for asteroids."

For now, 220P is heading back out to its furthest point from the sun, which is just inside the orbit of Jupiter at a distance of 4.68 astronomical units or 435 million miles (700 million kilometers). Having passed as close to Earth as it is going to get this time around on 12 October at a distance of 1.04 astronomical units or 97 million miles (156 million kilometres), the comet is currently magnitude +13 and fading. All eyes will be on 220P during its next time around the sun in late 2031.

The findings were published on Nov.3 in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

Keith Cooper is a freelance science journalist and editor in the United Kingdom, and has a degree in physics and astrophysics from the University of Manchester. He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.

#797. Isaiah Washington Debuts New Romance One Year After Wife’s Death

Grey’s Anatomy alum Isaiah Washington revealed he’s in a new relationship with content creator Kei Bennett one year after his wife Jenisa Garland’s death: “She is all mine now and I am all hers."

It’s a beautiful day for Isaiah Washington’s personal life.

More than a year after the Grey’s Anatomy alum shared wife Jenisa Garland had died suddenly in June 2025, he detailed his next chapter with content creator Kei Bennett.

“I have known many incredible women in my life,” Washington wrote on Instagram Nov. 17 alongside a photo of the new lady in his life, “but not a single one of them can hold a candle to the deep Southern charm of @keibenet.”

“I am not only thrilled to have gotten to know her in the last 9 months talking to her for hours every single day,” he wrote, “I am absolutely baffled how any man in her past could have harmed her, belittled her, disrespected her, or even betrayed her in the most deplorable ways.”

As for how she’s pulled at his heart strings?

“She has an incredible mind, heart, and spirit and I have grown to respect her intelligence, green thumb, hair stylist talent, entrepreneurship, holistic approach, and her black business owner's business acumen immensely,” he explained. “Yes, she has earned her place at my creative table and I love her dearly.”

And while Bennett may have kissed her fair share of frogs in the past, he feels they were all leading to her prince.

“I am so glad that all of the men who treated her like she was less than a Queen, all left her heartbroken, but not broken,” he wrote. “Don’t worry I will take it from here and I will never let her down as a friend and partner in love and creativity.”

“There has been no other woman who has made me laugh and has encouraged me as she has,” he added. “Yeah, I don't play about Kei Bennett, and just know that she doesn't play about me. Yeah…she is all mine now and I am all hers. Deal with it.”

And it’s clear Bennett is just as smitten, commenting under the post, “I love you to pieces. Thank you for this. My protector, my best friends, my love, Mousie’s poppop…you exceed every goal you set and have the most pure heart I’ve ever seen.”

The couple’s hard launch comes after Washington’s wife of 29 years died following a weeklong health battle in June 2025. Just last month, he shared deeper insight into the tragedy.

"It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family," Washington—dad to kids Isaiah, Tyme and Iman with Garland—captioned his Oct. 3 Instagram post. "She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered."

And while her death came as a shock to their family, Washington shared how grateful he was to have his three kids by his side during the devastating chapter. As he put it, "She has been gone 16 months now, but she left 3 incredibly amazing children behind to continue her legacy."

For a closer look into the love lives of more Grey’s Anatomy stars, keep reading…

After being introduced in 1995, Isaiah Washington knew pretty quickly that he wanted to scrub in with Jenisa Garland, the two tying the knot one year later.

"For me, being married and having children did change a lot of my trajectory," the actor, who starred as renowned cardiothoracic surgeon Preston Burke for three seasons of Grey's Anatomy, told Fox News Digital in 2022. "That's why I didn't want to get married 25 years ago, but I'm glad I did because the wife and children really make you the best human being that you can be."

Sadly, their 29-year marriage came to an untimely end when Garland—who shared kids Isaiah, Tyme and Iman with Washington—passed away in 2025.

"It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family," Washington wrote in an October 2026 Instagram post. "She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered."

But more than a year after the tragedy, Washington found love again with content creator Kei Bennett.

“She has an incredible mind, heart, and spirit and I have grown to respect her intelligence, green thumb, hair stylist talent, entrepreneurship, holistic approach, and her black business owner's business acumen immensely,” he explained in a November 2026 social media post. “Yes, she has earned her place at my creative table and I love her dearly.”

Looks like it was record producer Chris Ivery who asked series lead Ellen Pompeo to pick me, choose me, love me after they crossed paths at a Los Angeles grocery store in 2003.

"I was with my mutual friend," the actress—who's starred as Meredith Grey since the series' 2005 premiere—detailed during a 2022 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show.

So, after sharing a quick hello with her fellow Boston-area native, "He called me a bunch of times, and I wouldn't call him back. And then he said, 'You're rude. You won't call me back,' and I said, 'Well, because I'm not trying to go on a date with you.' And he said, 'Who's trying to go on a date with you? I don't even know you.'"

Basically, she continued, "We had a fight first. That's kind of always the way to my heart, is like, piss me off and I'm all yours."

Married four years later, the pair welcomed daughter Stella in 2009, her little sister Sienna in 2014 and son Christopher in 2016.

"We're sort of two kids who made it out and then landed in Hollywood and jumped on this ride," Pompeo said of their journey during a 2025 appearance on Alex Cooper's Call Her Daddy podcast. "We just couldn't believe that something was actually happening—that it was great, that I had this great job and we were getting to travel all over the world."

James Pickens Jr.'s starting line with wife Gina Taylor-Pickens dates back to the 1980s when the then-struggling actors met through the New York City theater scene. "I thought she was cute," the future chief medical officer Richard Webber explained to TV Fanatic, "and she gave me her number."

A stroll through Central Park proved to be the first steps of their forever. "We have a mantra that we've lived by for 35 years," the dad to Carl and Gavyn explained of the Deliver Us from Eva actress on a 2019 episode of Live with Kelly and Ryan. "Love unconditionally, forgive quickly and treat strife and trouble like a basket of rattlesnakes."

The romance between E.R. Fightmaster's neuroscientist Kai Bartley and Caterina Scorsone's neurosurgeon Amelia Shepherd may have been cut short during season 19, but as a wise woman once said, "If you aren’t willing to keep looking for light in the darkest of places without stopping, even when it seems impossible, you will never succeed."

And the skies certainly seemed sunny as Scorsone (mom to daughters Eliza, Pippa and Arwen with ex-husband Rob Giles) and Fightmaster strolled through L.A. in March 2026. Holding hands as they exited local mini-chain Highly Likely it seemed, uh, pretty certain that they were a couple.

While Ben Warren has switched in and out of scrubs as anesthesiologist turned firefighter turned surgical resident, Jason George, who starred on Grey's and its spin-off Station 19, has never wavered in his committment to writer wife Vandana Khanna.

Meeting at the University of Virginia, "She's my day one," he raved to Us Weekly of his bride, mom to Jasmine, Nikhil and Arun. "I've known this woman since before I knew I wanted to be an actor. I’ve known her over half my life. I’ve known her longer than I haven’t known her."

He shared his prescription for a decades-long union during a 2017 appearance on Steve Harvey's titular talk show.

"You're gonna have fights, because if you don't have fights, you're not being honest," he noted, stressing the importance of fighting fair. "When you settle it, don't say it's settled if it's not, and then bring it up again six months later."

Following marriages to Jane Parker and Arielle Goldrath, Kevin McKidd (a.k.a. army vet and recently departed head of trauma Owen Hunt) debuted a real-life crossover in November 2023, making his red carpet debut with Station 19 star Danielle Savre at the Global Down Syndrome Foundation's 15th Annual Be Beautiful Be Yourself Fashion Show.

The pairing "just kind of happened," the dad of four explained to People months later at The Walt Disney Company’s 2023 Emmy Awards Celebration. "We're really happy and she's an amazing human being, so I feel lucky on many levels in my life right now."

Crossing paths with French filmmaker Manu Boyer at a New York swimming pool, Kim Raver decided to fully dive in. "That first meeting is kind of sacred," she detailed to Women's Health in 2005, "so I think I want to keep it to myself."

Though she was willing to share how her husband—the two share sons Luke and Leo—helped her prepare for cardiothoracic surgeon Teddy Altman's first intimate encounter with onscreen love Cass Beckman (Sophia Bush).

With Raver also tasked with directing the scene, "I couldn't tell whether he was like, 'This is awesome,' or, 'Wait, how are you going to do this?'" she admitted to People. "And I was like, 'This is how we're going to do it.'"

Camilla Luddington and Matthew Alan's first date to a 2008 The Temper Trap concert proved to be a moment, a love, a dream, aloud. Because 11 years after that initial outing—and two after the actors welcomed their daughter Hayden in 2017—they wed in front of 70 loved ones in Santa Barbara, Calif., with Luddington walking down the aisle to the band's hit "Sweet Disposition."

As the British star, who's embodied general surgeon-turned OB/GYN resident Dr. Jo Wilson since 2012, put it to People at the time, "We're just ready to do the damn thing. We kind of already feel married because we have a 2-year-old. But there's something romantic to us about solidifying that family unit by having the ceremony and actually having Hayden present."

And following their 2019 vows, she added, "I'm just excited to get into that new normal of married life."

That included adding to their roster, she and the Castle Rock actor welcoming son Lucas in August 2020.

Chris Carmack has unique insight on how his orthopedic surgeon Atticus "Link" Lincoln fell for longtime friend Jo. He and now-wife Erin Slaver spent the first year of their relationship as friends after meeting at a cast party for Nashville. (The concert violinist, touring fiddler and vocalist appeared on the series as a backup singer and also played in series star Sam Palladio's band.)

"We met, maybe there was some attraction, it didn't make sense at the time," Slaver explained in a March 2026 video on their YouTube channel. Agreed Carmack, in a relationship at the time, "You were off-limits for me for a minute."

After they "floated around in the same circles for a year," noted Carmack, they started dating, marrying in 2018, two years after they welcomed daughter Kai. Youngest daughter Cielle joined the band in 2022.

Since 1984, Debbie Allen has been huddled up with former NBA point guard Norm Nixon. But the pair didn't become instant teammates after meeting on the set of The Fish That Saved Pittsburgh in 1979.

"She went to New York and moved to Fame, and I went back to Los Angeles," the athlete recounted to Trib Total Media. "We stayed in touch, and I realized I had more fun with her than any of the other women I was dating."

As the Debbie Allen Dance Academy founder—who's appeared as world-class urologist and board chairman Catherine Fox since 2011—put it, they're usually in sync.

"I think our relationship has always been born on friendship and commonality in terms of things that we both like," the mom to Vivian, Norman Jr. and Nixon's son DeVaughn told People in 2024, noting they both like "to read books. We both like to go to the movies. We both like to travel. We both love our children."

Decades in, "We've hit some rocks and hit some walls," she acknowledged. "But at the end of the day, we really love each other and we sleep together every night and we love our family."

Safe to say Harry Shum Jr.'s first date with now-wife Shelby Rabara was a dream.

"We both cried and it was just such a beautiful experience because after that we just talked about you," he told Jennifer Hudson during a 2022 appearance on her talk show of their Dreamgirls viewing. "It really kinda brought us together and we opened up about a lot of things and it was just such a beautiful first date."

Naturally, there was no way they could ever go. The Glee alum (who plays recently fired resident Benson Kwan) and the Steven Universe star wed in November 2015, welcoming daughter Xia four years later.

Transplant surgeon Nick Marsh has proven to be Meredith's person since entering the Grey's universe in 2018. But off-camera it's fiancée Lindsay Rae Hofmann who's stolen Speedman's heart.

Engaged since 2023, the Felicity alum and the co-founder of swimwear brand Juillet welcomed daughter Pfeiffer in 2021 and son Indy in 2024. And she's provided quite the assist to his growing television career.

"She started watching You, and then I ended up on that show," he explained to Esquire in 2021. "She started binge-watching Grey's Anatomy on Netflix during the pandemic, and here I am. Whatever she seems to watch, I seem to end up on."

#796. Israel row a 'defining moment for us' - Hallgrimsson

Heimir Hallgrimsson celebrates the victory over Kosovo with Harvey Vale

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson says the controversy surrounding the Nations League games against Israel has made "this group stronger".

The players took a vote on whether to play the two matches - in September and October - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war, with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

The Republic of Ireland won the first match 3-0 in Hungary before a 1-1 draw in Serbia.

Hallgrimsson was speaking after his side defeated 10-man Kosovo 3-0 in Dublin on Tuesday night to finish runners-up to Austria in Group B3.

The second place means the Republic of Ireland will be in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw next month and also ensures they have a promotion/relegation play-off in March against a League A team as they try to move up to the top tier for the first time.

"It tested everyone - physically, mentally and no I've learned a lot doubt and the players have learned a lot and grown," said Hallgrimsson.

"I am pretty sure in one year, two years when this team becomes successful we will look back and say that was the defining moment for us.

"I am pretty sure we will look back in hindsight and say this was a huge moment for us.

"Us as leaders sometimes artificially create us against the world to get the group to stick together and I have said we have got that environment for free for two or three weeks and we survived it and it made this team and this group stronger."

Republic of Ireland seal second with win over 10-man Kosovo

Talisman Parrott caps dream year with two more goals

Republic of Ireland denied by Israel in draw

Troy Parrott scored two penalties and Jack Moylan also netted against a Kosovo team hit by the dismissal of Kreshnik Hajrizi after 26 minutes.

It brought to an end a campaign which saw the Republic of Ireland win two matches, with two drawn and two lost.

"We know we will never be perfect and we are trying to find a way to win with what we have," Hallgrimsson added.

"I think we are getting better and better on that. Like I said in the first meeting when I was here and was introduced, I said I want to build a team that is difficult to play against and I feel like we are getting closer and closer to that.

"We are now consistent in our selection of players. We've more or less found our squad, our group and with doing that on a consistent basis, playing the same players together, playing the same system, the connections between players are starting to emerge."

The promotion/relegation play-off draw take place on Friday with the Republic set to go up against one of Croatia, Serbia, Denmark or Wales.

"Everybody, and especially us, like to play the top teams. For one, to compare yourself with the best teams, that's one thing," he said.

"Second, those teams will expose your weaknesses and that helps you in your growth to play these teams and they will expose your weaknesses so we can continue our growth. We're already looking forward to March.

"[There are] exciting teams in the pot. Whoever we draw, it's going to be two tough games and it's good for this team at this time to play these matches instead of friendlies, for example.

"So we're really excited for March and looking forward to meeting the players again."

#795. Joe Jonas Reveals Cheeky Gift He Recently Gave Ex Demi Lovato

Joe Jonas recently revealed that he gave Demi Lovato, whom he dated briefly in 2010, a cheeky birthday gift that nodded toward one of her most viral interview moments.

Joe Jonas’ favorite meme? He would have to say mug.

More than 10 years after Demi Lovato went viral for revealing mugs were her “favorite dish” during an interview with NRJ Berlin, her Camp Rock costar—whom she dated briefly in 2010—revealed it’s still his favorite pop culture moment.

“It’s amazing,” Joe told his brothers Kevin Jonas and Nick Jonas during the Nov. 17 episode of their Hey Jonas! podcast. “I bought her a mug as a gift for coming as our special guest recently or her birthday. I think I sent her a mug for her birthday. I can’t remember.”

Meanwhile, Kevin and Joe agreed it was a great clip.  As Kevin emphasized, “She wasn’t incorrect.”

For Demi’s part, she recently revealed that she intentionally had misinterpreted the question—the interviewer was referring to food rather than cookware—but she opted to answer it in her own way.

“I had been asked so many questions that day,” Demi reflected during an appearance on Keke Palmer’s Baby, It’s Keke Palmer podcast in March. “I was doing, like, a press tour and you get bored doing press tours.”

And so, the Disney Channel alum joked she thought at the time, “‘I’m gonna start f--king with the interviewers.’”

“I just ran with it,” Demi joked, emphasizing that only part of the interview went viral. “In the long, extended video, you see me look at my tour manager and like smirk. Like, ‘did you catch that one?’ And then that went viral and everyone thought I was serious.”

But there’s nothing wrong with being confident in answering the question this way, especially given Demi made a worthy case for mugs.

“I like mugs because they’re very comfortable in your hand,” she said in the now-viral clip. “And they hold hot things that you don’t have to touch. So, you know, coffee or hot tea.”

As for Joe running so far with the joke that he sent his ex a mug as a present? While Demi previously joked she was “mad” at Joe following their breakup, there’s no longer any mean mugging between them.

“It’s been such a wonderful relationship through so many years,” Joe told USA Today earlier this year after he and Demi each made appearances at each other’s respective concerts. “I feel so grateful that Demi and I can go perform together still and see each other in these different journeys of our life.”

For more Disney alums who dated, keep reading…

Disney Channel worlds collided after Sabrina Carpenter met Bradley Steven Perry.

The Girl Meets World star and Good Luck Charlie actor’s romance began in 2014, when Carpenter’s show began filming right next door to Perry’s Mighty Med.

“[It was a] really unique way to ask someone out,” Carpenter told J-14 at the time, describing a scene out of a pirate flick: “Like, they do the little bottles and they put notes in them and send them across the ocean, like one of those, and [he] put a note inside. It was cute.”

Though they broke up in 2015, Perry—who married Candace Cameron Bure’s daughter Natasha Bure in 2025—noted that their connection was a sweet young love.

“Sabrina was my first girlfriend,” Perry said during an appearance on the Unplanned Podcast in 2024. “We dated for about two years.”

He added, “It was very much like a little high school relationship.”

Bella Thorne and Gregg Sulkin shook up young Hollywood when they first stepped out together in 2015.

But the Shake It Up alum and Wizards of Waverly Place actor went their separate ways a year later.

“Our schedules made seeing each other difficult," Thorne and Sulkin told People in a joint statement back in 2016, “and we decided that for now this would be best.”

But they’ll always look back on their fairytale romance with a smile.

“After much thought and soul-searching, we have made the difficult decision to end our relationship,” they added. “We will always love each other and have a deep respect for one another, as we have each grown to be better people because of our time together.”

Can you imagine what would happen if Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens never dated?

The High School Musical alums hit it off as soon as the cameras started rolling for the franchise’s first film in 2005.

“We created a bond right from the start,” Hudgens—who played the Gabriella Montez to Efron’s Troy Bolton in the films—told People in 2022. “We were like, ‘We’re doing this, it’s us or nothing.’”

“It started off really organically,” she added. “I could not have been more grateful to have that relationship at that time.”

And while the pair eventually had to go their own ways, you can still bet on the fact that they had a next-level connection.

Nick Jonas and Selena Gomez’s romance was burnin’ up from 2008 to 2010.

And while they shared two years together, Gomez’s real prize from the relationship would have to be her unbreakable bond with BFF Taylor Swift.”

“Taylor and I dated the Jonas Brothers,” Gomez—who married Benny Blanco in 2025—said during a 2025 episode of the Therapuss with Jake Shane podcast of how she and Swift met. “I dated Nick and she dated Joe [Jonas]. And everything  was cute, we were young. We all know and love each other now and it’s so cute.”

Gomez added of her relationship with Jonas, dad to daughter Malti with wife Priyanka Chopra, “She and I like to say the best thing we got out of those relationships was each other because it was really sweet.”

At one point, Miley Cyrus thought Dylan Sprouse could be the one.

Indeed, the Hannah Montana alum revealed she and The Suite Life of Zack & Cody star were much more than work colleagues.

“Dylan Sprouse was my boyfriend,” Cyrus told Alex Cooper during the March 2026 Disney+ Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special. “I think he was the cutest.”

Responding to past rumors that she and Sprouse—who married model Barbara Palvin in 2023—were an item, the “Flowers” singer added, “It's true, confirmed.”

But during their brief romance, she also got to spend quality time with Sprouse’s twin brother Cole Sprouse—though she knew she couldn’t have the best of both worlds.

“Dylan was my crush,” Cyrus continued. “Their dad would take us to sushi. I was into the whole culture, and it was a two-for-one. Like, bring the brother. Hello!”

Joe Jonas and Demi Lovato may be like Venus and Mars, but they were once on the same astral plane.

“Demi and I knew going into our romantic relationship that it may not be an easy one,” Jonas told Us Weekly in 2025. “I realize over the time we have shared together that I feel I care more about our friendship right now.”

That’s why the Jonas Brothers member wouldn’t change a thing about the love story he shared with Lovato—who married Jordan “Jutes” Lutes in 2025.

"T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon. Everyone is very confident on this."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out.

T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle.

"T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued.

Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth.

"The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold."

Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event.

"There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the Goddard Spaceflight Center, told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption."

Hays notes that the intense light from the red giant dramatically outshines the dimmer white dwarf, making detailed observation challenging. There is also no way to precisely measure the temperature and pressure of the matter lurking near the surface of the smaller star. "Predicting nova explosions are a little like predicting the weather; conditions may be right but the timing of the storm can be uncertain."

There'll be no visual warning of the eruption before it reaches Earth, though according to Hays there could be an early flash of light in the X-ray spectrum.

"The world's amateur astronomers have been doing an awesome job of keeping T CrB under hair-trigger monitoring roughly every minute or two, so when T CrB has brightened by around one magnitude, then alerts will spread around the world within minutes," said Schaefer.

Once the call goes out, telescopes and observatories around the world will kick into gear, running pre-prepared observation programmes to capitalize on the rare and cataclysmic event. "When the nuclear runaway process starts, it will take off and peak very quickly, in less than a day."

The nova will see the star jump from its normal brightness of magnitude +10 — which is beyond the detection limit of the naked eye — to magnitude +1.7, making it appear as if a star brighter than the North Star Polaris has suddenly burst to life in the night sky.

"The brightness will fall below naked-eye visibility in dark places within a couple of days and become too faint for binoculars within about a week," said Hays. "Outside the visible band, for example, in radio, X-ray and gamma rays, light caused by the eruption will be visible for months or even years. "

T CrB can be found glowing close to the magnitude +4.28 star Epsilon Coronae Borealis in the constellation Corona Borealis during the early evening in November, with the constellations of Hercules and Bootes on either side.

It will dip below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. just a few hours after sunset, before re-emerging into the northeastern sky in the predawn hours.

Want to capture a photo of T. CrB when it erupts? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing the night sky, along with our picks of the best cameras, lenses and smart telescopes that are perfect for capturing the majesty of the starry realm.

Anthony Wood joined Space.com in April 2025 after contributing articles to outlets including IGN, New Atlas and Gizmodo. He has a passion for the night sky, science, Hideo Kojima, and human space exploration, and can’t wait for the day when astronauts once again set foot on the moon.

#793. Ward close to new Republic of Ireland deal as World Cup chance beckons

Carla Ward was appointed Republic of Ireland manager in January 2025

Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says she is close to agreeing a contract extension, as she named her squad for their 2027 Women's World Cup play-off final with Poland.

The former Aston Villa manager replaced Eileen Gleeson at the helm in January 2025 and has led the side to promotion to League A in the Nations League and their highest ever position in the Uefa rankings.

The Republic of Ireland have lost just one of their past six games and now face Poland in a play-off for a spot at the World Cup in Brazil next summer.

Ward's side travel to Gdansk for the first leg on 1 December before the reverse fixture four days later at Dublin's Aviva Stadium.

The 42-year-old's current deal expires at the end of the 2027 World Cup qualification cycle.

Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said earlier this month that there were "live conversations" around Ward's contract.

"I want to get one thing straight - last time I said I wanted to focus on the next four games," said Ward.

"What I mean by that is, I want the focus to be on the players and certainly not myself.

"But what I can say to everybody is, I think you all know that I love being here. I want to be here. I have absolutely no intention of going anywhere.

"Thankfully, the FAI feel the same. So yes, just to echo David's words, we're close. And look, we're happy. I'm happy. So, yeah, I'm sure you'll have me for a little bit longer."

Ward in talks over Republic of Ireland contract extension

Saoirse Noonan returns to the Republic of Ireland squad for the Poland games after sitting out the play-off semi-final victory over Kazakhstan because of an ankle injury.

The Watford forward comes in for Jess Ziu, who has a shin injury, in the only change to the squad.

Ward said that "now is not the time for trying new things" with the squad, which includes Crystal Palace midfielder Shanade Hopcroft after her first call-up for the Kazakhstan games.

Republic of Ireland secured 3-1 and 1-0 victories over the Poles when the sides met in World Cup qualifiers in April.

Poland edged out Belgium on penalties in their semi-final and Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor poses a dangerous attacking threat.

"They're a top side, they're a really good side," added Ward.

"They've proven that. They've got arguably one of the best forwards in the world and I think that their performance against Belgium was superb, home and away. I think they were excellent.

"They created a lot. We're under no illusions that this is going to be easy because we've won two games of football against them.

"I think both sides will tweak a few things naturally because we'll both want to try and win the game. But I go back to if we focus on us, what we're good at, if we execute our game plan and everything we want to do, then I think that we can win the game."

While Rob Kardashian is mostly absent from his family’s Hulu series The Kardashians, his recent camo on a Prime Video series has a sweet nod to dad Robert Kardashian Sr.’s family.

Rob Kardashian is kicking his latest rare reality TV appearance into gear.

While his sisters are fixture of pop culture with their Hulu series The Kardashians, Rob has managed to stay mostly out of the spotlight in recent years. However, he made a rare exception for the latest episode of Fully Torqued Unleashed.

In the third episode of season three of the Prime Video series, which dropped Nov. 7, Rob makes a brief cameo to ask host Steve Pazamy to assist in a surprise for his father Robert Kardashian Sr.’s cousin Cici Bussey. The 39-year-old expressed that he wants to fix up Cici’s 1963 Mercedes, which she has owned over 20 years.

Later, Cici is floored by the gift and expressed her gratitude on camera.

However, there is one part of filming that Rob does enjoy—enough to even bring him back from time to time.

Nevertheless, he admitted, “The reason I don't is because I'm a homebody and I just choose, like I said, my peace and happiness.”

#791. Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

Racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious. In 1941, Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler himself compared Eastern Europe to "Germany's India" after the British colonial model, declaring that "like the English, we shall rule this empire with a handful of men."

But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.

This is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust. Others have argued that the intense focus on the Nazi era has, at least in part, come at the expense of a meaningful reckoning with Germany's colonial history.

"I do think this is nonsense," says Stephan Malinowski, a Professor of Modern European History at the University of Edinburgh. "If it were true, then all other colonial countries who are not discussing the Holocaust, like Great Britain for example, or France or Spain or Portugal, they would then supposedly be very, very attentive to colonial crimes and to colonial history, which it seems to me is not the case."

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence," a new exhibition at the German Historical Museum in Berlin curated by Malinowski, does not aim to settle the debate but to tell its story.

The exhibition begins with a hippopotamus-hide whip used in African colonies displayed alongside a canister of Zyklon B, the poison used in Nazi gas chambers. The juxtaposition highlights the contrast between colonial violence and the industrialized mass murder of the Holocaust. Yet it also points to connections: Whips were used in Nazi concentration camps, while Fascist Italy deployed chemical weapons against civilians and soldiers during its invasion of Ethiopia (then Abyssinia) in 1935-36.

In the 1930s, anti-colonial thinkers from India to the Caribbean argued that colonialism and fascism were two sides of the same coin. "There is nothing new or original about the blustering exploits of Hitler and Mussolini," observed the Trinidadian journalist and Pan-Africanist George Padmore in 1938. "They have all been used before by the British in their efforts to obtain the subjection of less powerfully armed and more industrially backward people."

European colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence. In "The Origins of Totalitarianism" (1951), German-American philosopher Hannah Arendt argued that colonial territories served as laboratories for racial ideologies and practices of domination that could be applied beyond the legal constraints of Europe. Arendt described how these later "boomeranged" back into Europe and helped shape totalitarian politics in distinct and unprecedented form.

The Congo Free State, King Leopold II of Belgium's private colony from 1885 to 1908, became notorious for its extreme brutality, as colonial authorities used executions, amputations and sexual violence to ensure rubber production quotas were met. Forced labor was also central to Nazi rule, with millions of Poles, Ukrainians, Russians and others from the Soviet Union, and Jews, subjected to exploitation and "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" ("extermination through work"). Within a few years, the regime mobilized around 13 to 14 million forced laborers, a scale comparable to the transatlantic slave trade over more than three centuries. The Nazis sought to extract value from their victims at every stage, confiscating their property, exploiting their labor, and even harvesting gold teeth and hair from the dead.

While racism underpinned both colonial empires and Nazism, Malinowski says the goals were different. The colonial powers tended to present assimilation as a path to advancement, forcing colonized people to adopt European culture, serve imperial interests, and suggesting that a select, educated few could gain opportunities at elite institutions such as Oxford or Cambridge. "This is definitely not something that the Nazi regime is offering to Poles or to Russians or let alone to Jews," added Malinowski.

"In terms of violence, colonial violence was just as extreme as Nazi violence. But Nazi violence was annihilatory and exterminatory compared to colonial violence in the colonies," says Edward Kissi, a historian at the School of Interdisciplinary Global Studies at the University of South Florida. He points to the example of how, unlike European colonial powers in Africa, the Nazis pursued the elimination of Black-Germans or peoples of African descent in Germany through forced sterilization. "Even in racism, colonial color-based racism and colonial anti-Jewish sentiments were fundamentally different from what the Nazis pursued."

On October 2, 1904, German General Lothar von Trotha issued the "Vernichtungsbefehl" ("extermination order") following the Herero uprising in German South West Africa (present-day Namibia). Historians generally attribute the order to a combination of racial ideology, a desire to terrorize the population into submission, and efforts to secure colonial control over land, labor and resources. Between 1904 and 1908, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 Herero (around 80% of the population) and 10,000 (around half the population) Nama died.

One area where the exhibition draws no direct parallel is the industrialized killing carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and Auschwitz-Birkenau. "Where the two things really diverge is the Holocaust and is the systematic mass murder of the European Jews and it's murder for the very purpose of murder," explains Malinowski. The deportation of around 1,800 Jews from the Greek islands of Rhodes and Kos in July 1944 illustrates how Nazi persecution often defied military or economic logic. Even after the war was effectively lost, the community was transported to Auschwitz, where most were murdered immediately upon arrival.

The issue of the "singularity" of the Holocaust came to the fore during the 1980s "Historikerstreit" ("historians' dispute"). Historian Ernst Nolte argued that Nazism should be understood in the wider context of 20th-century political violence, and as a response to Bolshevik terror in particular. Critics accused him of downplaying German responsibility for Nazi crimes.

Since 2020, a renewed debate dubbed the "Historikerstreit 2.0" has focused on whether the Holocaust should be viewed as a unique reference point in German memory culture or be understood alongside the histories of colonialism, racism and empire. The dispute now is less about the legitimacy of comparison than about its implications.

The mass murder of tens of thousands of the Herero and Nama during four years of German colonial rule is now regarded as the first genocide of the 20th-century. In 2016, Nama representatives walked out of talks after Germany's chief negotiator said what happened was "incomparable" to the Holocaust. The German government has since recognized the events as genocide "from today's perspective," but it has not yet accepted legal liability or agreed to pay formal reparations.

Martinican intellectual Aime Cesaire argued in "Discourse on Colonialism" (1950) that Europe condemned under Nazism forms of violence it had long accepted in its colonies. The exhibition opens amid renewed debates over settler colonialism, the definition of genocide, and the meaning of "never again," sharpened by Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice over German support for Israel during the war in Gaza. These tensions are reflected in visitors' comments in the exhibition's epilogue, even though the exhibition itself does not address Israel or Palestine beyond a reference to Mohammed Amin al-Husseini, appointed Grand Mufti of Jerusalem in 1921.

Germany has unequivocally accepted responsibility for the Holocaust, which is front and center of the country's culture of remembrance.  However, Kissi likens Germany's apparent reluctance to reckon with its colonial history to debates in the US over slavery, in Cambodia over the Khmer Rouge, and in Turkey over the Armenian genocide. According to him, Germany's contemporary identity cannot be fully understood without examining its colonial history and the ways the Nazis appropriated and transformed aspects of that legacy. "I think Germans and all other human beings who have experienced violent pasts and difficult pasts should be very careful not to delink or dissociate those facts from their present," Kissi said. "These are historical patterns. It is better to deal with these historical patterns and discomforts than to just fight them and then say this has absolutely nothing to do with German national identity."

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence" is on show at the German Historical Museum until April 11, 2027.

#790. From kit boy to manager at 28 - Dumbarton appoint Fellowes

Martin Fellowes has become the youngest manager in SPFL history, taking on the Dumbarton head coach job at the age of 28.

Leaving his position as assistant manager and head of football operations at Scottish League 2 leaders Stranraer, Fellowes inherits a team six places further down the ladder.

With experience on the Scotland Under-19s coaching team, Fellowes spent almost 10 years with East Kilbride, rising from teenage kit boy to a two-month spell as interim manager in 2023, winning the Lowland League Cup.

With a day job in office furniture sales, he holds a Uefa A licence.

"You have to earn people's respect as a person," Fellowes told BBC Scotland.

"When you are a young guy and you're leading a football club, I don't think you can come in and change everything and lead with an iron fist.

"You have to get people's respect on and off the pitch. I know there will be plenty of criticism and there will be plenty of people sitting here today doubting that I'm capable of doing this job at 28.

"But now really the work for me has started on, by the end of the process, having gained those people onside to say, 'he was more than capable of doing this job and we're delighted to have him here'.

"I can only do that through winning games of football."

Martin Fellowes (right) as a 17-year-old kit man at East Kilbride

Jim Duffy was 29 when he began his long managerial career at Falkirk and Rhys McCabe was player/manager at Airdrieonians at the same age.

Ian Cathro, now leading French club Saint-Etienne, took charge of Hearts when he was just 30.

Fellowes replaces Frank McKeown, who resigned last month, while director of football Danny Lennon had been standing in on an interim basis.

The Sons are two points off the promotion places and visit Spartans on Saturday.

"We're not going to reinvent the wheel," Fellowes added.

"We're not going to do anything that anybody else hasn't been doing.

"But if we can add the 5% to every different department and win games of football, I think over time people will understand that sometimes the age isn't a barrier but it can actually be an advantage."

#789. Mandy Moore’s Ex-Husband Ryan Adams, 52, Engaged to Kate Farr, 22

Ryan Adams—who was married to Mandy Moore from 2009 to 2016—announced his engagement to 22-year-old musician Kate Farr: “I’ve never been happier in my life.”

Ryan Adams wants everybody to know about his new chapter with Kate Farr.

After all, the “Wonderwall” singer revealed that he and the 22-year-old are engaged after six months of dating.

“I’ve never been happier in my life,” Adams told TMZ Nov. 17. “Kate is the most fascinating, kindest nerd I’ve ever met. She’s my best friend, and I’ve never been happier. Here’s to love.”

Before meeting Farr, Adams, 52, tied the knot with Mandy Moore in 2009 following a two-year courtship. However, the couple ultimately went their separate ways, finalizing their divorce in 2016.

Though Moore, 42, has since married husband Taylor Goldsmith—with whom she shares kids Gus, 5, Ozzie, 4, and Lou, 2—she’s been candid about her relationship with the “Everybody Knows” singer.

"I felt like I was drowning,” she shared during a 2019 appearance on Marc Maron's WTF podcast. "It was so untenable and unsustainable and it was so lonely. I was so sad. I was so lonely with him.”

And for Moore, that was a sign she wasn’t in the right relationship.

“I knew that this wasn't the rest of my life,” she continued. “I knew that this wasn't the person I was supposed to be with, I knew that I wasn't the person I was meant to be."

That same year, the This Is Us star—along with a group of other women in the music industry, including Phoebe Bridgers—accused Adams of emotional abuse, alleging that the music producer impacted their careers with manipulation tactics.

"Music was a point of control for him," Moore said in a New York Times interview. "He would always tell me, 'You're not a real musician, because you don't play an instrument.'"

Moore alleged, "His controlling behavior essentially did block my ability to make new connections in the industry during a very pivotal and potentially lucrative time—my entire mid-to-late 20s."

Though Adams initially denied the allegations at the time, he issued an apology the following year for his actions.

“All I can say is that I’m sorry,” he wrote in a 2020 letter to Daily Mail. “It’s that simple. This period of isolation and reflection made me realize that I needed to make significant changes in my life.”

The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds.

When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use.

Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001.

When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later.

"In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus."

The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO.

During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions.

"One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website.
